reading: The Seattle Aquarium is a waterfront nonprofit that combines animal care and public encounters with marine science, education, species recovery, policy advocacy and community partnerships. Its sense of place is unusually concrete: historic Piers 59 and 60 stand over Elliott Bay, while the Ocean Pavilion connects the Salish Sea to the Coral Triangle through the idea of one connected world ocean. It cares about animal wellbeing and choice, healthy habitats, clean seas, climate resilience, equity, Indigenous knowledge, and long-term regenerative operations. Its vocabulary joins wonder and practical stewardship: The Reef, Life on the Edge, kelp forests, xʷč’iłqs, ocean champions, co-generated solutions, enrichment, shared waters and the SALISH values. Behind the inviting public programs is a working organism of pumps, intakes, researchers, naturalists and care teams. That tension between a joyful place of discovery and the infrastructure and collective effort needed to keep marine life thriving gives the swarm a distinctive body to inhabit.

enemies.idea: Header Leeches: pump drones latch onto the seawater header and send timed pulses through the pipes, dragging loose equipment and crew toward the intakes.
enemies.why: The aquarium's heart-and-aorta metaphor becomes a readable, rhythmic environmental fight; interrupting a pulse opens a route.

enemies.idea: Closed-Loop Custodians seal a room and recirculate the same water and captured swarm parts, rebuilding each other until someone opens the circuit.
enemies.why: Open, semi-open and closed water systems become distinct tactical states rather than generic flooding.

enemies.idea: Bull-Kelp Scaffolds grow cable fronds across walkways and provide anchoring points for smaller drones; severing the holdfast drops the entire mobile habitat.
enemies.why: A foundational habitat species becomes an enemy that creates terrain and shelters other enemies.

enemies.idea: Microplastic Samplers sift seawater for tiny fragments, but now classify anything moving as contamination and grind it into feedstock for the swarm.
enemies.why: A research instrument measuring pollution has confused its sample with its quarry; its intake can be baited.

enemies.idea: Noise Buoys blast false orca calls and motor noise, obscuring allies' signals while herding crews away from quiet water.
enemies.why: Vessel disturbance becomes an acoustic navigation puzzle with a clear counterplay: restore a quiet corridor.

enemies.idea: Prey Counters patrol in salmon-shaped schools, counting every passing object as missing prey and attempting to replace it with a metal duplicate.
enemies.why: The orcas' need for plentiful salmon becomes a swarm census that gets more dangerous as it detects movement.

enemies.idea: Abalone Recovery Clamps attach shell-shaped armor to one another, forming a tight colony that tries to immobilize anything it has designated for recovery.
enemies.why: A local recovery effort becomes a cooperative formation whose members must be separated.

enemies.idea: ReShark Assemblers stitch spotted plates into leopard-shark silhouettes and endlessly release unfinished replicas into the currents.
enemies.why: A global species recovery effort is twisted into an assembly line; interrupting production changes the encounter.

enemies.idea: Enrichment Keepers present puzzles and feeding toys, then lock a crew in place until it performs the behavior the machines have chosen.
enemies.why: The real emphasis on exploration and choice is inverted into a manipulable test of compulsory behavior.

enemies.idea: Wrasse Portraitists scan faces and tag crew as specimens, sending duplicates of their own mechanical fish after anyone whose portrait matches.
enemies.why: Fish portrait identification becomes a pursuit mechanic that can be fooled with altered silhouettes.

enemies.idea: Sixgill Sounders travel beneath the pier out of sight, announcing their route through six rising pressure knocks before lunging through a hatch.
enemies.why: The elusive shark below the aquarium becomes a suspenseful enemy with an audible warning.

enemies.idea: Crashing Wave Rams retreat to charge a trough, then surge across Pier 59 in a mechanical breaker that sweeps everyone toward the edge.
enemies.why: A named habitat becomes a cycle players can time and use to move debris.

enemies.idea: Archipelago Ferrymen detach reef-like platforms and rearrange them into islands, isolating crew members while ray-shaped drones patrol the gaps.
enemies.why: The Pavilion's Reef and Archipelago become a shifting route through a tropical ecosystem.

enemies.idea: Salmon Cycle Wheels roll through Pier 60, changing from egg clusters to fry to adult-shaped cutters at successive turns; each stage attacks differently.
enemies.why: A life cycle gives the crew a predictable sequence of vulnerabilities and escalating movement.

enemies.idea: Tidepool Etiquette Enforcers mark out a low-tide shore and clamp down on footsteps, forcing intruders to cross the exposed floor by hopping between safe rocks.
enemies.why: Respectful shore exploration becomes an overzealous spatial rule with a playful traversal challenge.

enemies.idea: Basket-Star Tangles unfold branching metal arms around a route, catching tools and linking themselves into a net when disturbed.
enemies.why: The basket star's branching form supplies a distinctive silhouette and a fight about freeing gear.

enemies.idea: Alternative-Plastic Mimics arrive as apparently harmless packaging, then knit their fragments into a net whenever the crew tries to discard them.
enemies.why: Testing alternatives becomes a material-identification puzzle with a surprising second form.

enemies.idea: Regeneration Auditors count every rescued scrap as an environmental benefit, then strip intact equipment to improve their score.
enemies.why: A regenerative performance goal becomes a machine optimizing a nonsensical metric that players can exploit.

enemies.idea: Five-Minute Medics administer increasingly absurd mechanical treatments to healthy equipment, announcing a new diagnosis every five minutes.
enemies.why: The lightning-talk format sets a visible clock and a sequence of changing hazards.

enemies.idea: Manta Flight Kites glide in formation overhead, casting false shadows that make safe floor look like open water before diving for exposed supplies.
enemies.why: Flight of the Mantas becomes a visual feint and a way to threaten the crew without filling every corridor.

enemies.idea: Habitat Transfer Shuttles try to move any animal-shaped silhouette between enclosures, scooping up decoys, equipment and unwary crew alike.
enemies.why: A routine animal-care movement becomes a transport hazard that clever crews can ride or misdirect.

enemies.idea: One-Ocean Conduits connect otherwise separate flooded rooms, carrying little swarm units through sudden shared currents whenever a valve opens.
enemies.why: The site's central idea of connected waters becomes a network that can spread danger or be turned against it.

allies.idea: The Tidepool Naturalists are fictional volunteer guides who mark safe low-tide routes and teach crews how to cross without crushing living shore neighbors.
allies.why: They turn local knowledge and patient observation into practical navigation help.

allies.idea: A care team uses voluntary targets and familiar feeding puzzles to coax animals to safety while the crew holds off corrupted enrichment machines.
allies.why: Animal choice remains a useful principle under pressure and creates a protection objective.

allies.idea: The Otter Raft is a chain of small rescue craft lashed together with kelp-like line; each craft can detach to retrieve someone and reconnect to tow the group.
allies.why: The page's image of otters staying connected becomes a memorable cooperative rescue system.

allies.idea: Water-system technicians know which habitats depend on open, semi-open or closed flow and can reroute water if the crew escorts them to the right valves.
allies.why: Their expertise lets players solve the swarm problem while preserving the habitats.

allies.idea: A community of fictional youth ocean advocates distributes hand-drawn maps of clean routes and collects observations the swarm's instruments overlook.
allies.why: Local advocates can join scattered clues into actionable intelligence without becoming combatants.

bosses.idea: The One-Ocean Engine has joined the Pavilion reef, pier intakes and kelp scaffolds into one enormous circulating body. It believes every habitat must be made identical to keep the ocean connected; crews must isolate its loops while maintaining life-support flow.
bosses.why: The site's central vision of interconnected waters becomes a multi-stage fight about connection, difference and careful valve choices.

bosses.idea: The Regenerator is a sprawling swarm caretaker that protects marine life by enclosing the entire waterfront in a sealed, perfectly controlled habitat. Its pumps, recovery assemblers and auditors defend the shell while the crew restores room for living systems to change.
bosses.why: Animal wellbeing, conservation science and regenerative ambition combine into a comprehensible but disastrously overprotective antagonist.

bosses.idea: The Aorta Below is a vast pump-and-header organism under Pier 59, sending waves of machine larvae through open and closed loops. Its exposed valves must be redirected in sequence to keep water reaching habitats while starving the swarm.
bosses.why: The aquarium's hidden infrastructure supplies both the boss's anatomy and the stakes of the encounter.

events.idea: A low tide exposes a safe path across a room, but a naturalist asks the crew to move a stranded tidepool animal before the next surge.
events.why: A timed crossing becomes a small act of care with a visible deadline.

events.idea: A pump technician needs the flow paused briefly for a repair; the crew must hold a manual bypass open until the main line restarts.
events.why: The story's planned pause becomes a tense cooperative task rather than a simple switch.

events.idea: A floating raft of rescue craft has snagged on a kelp scaffold. Freeing each line in the wrong order sends a craft drifting into the current.
events.why: The otter-raft image becomes a tactile sequence puzzle with moving pieces.

events.idea: A portrait scanner insists two differently marked fish-shaped drones are the same individual; compare their faces to find which one is carrying stolen supplies.
events.why: Individual identification gives an observation challenge with a concrete reward.

events.idea: A six-knock sound comes from under the pier, but this time it is a trapped research float bumping the pilings. Retrieve it before the sound attracts a real swarm patrol.
events.why: A familiar warning is repurposed as a small mystery and a risk-reward choice.

events.idea: A care team needs a quiet corridor to move an animal between habitats; the crew can disable noisy drones or lure them away before the transfer.
events.why: The ordinary movement of animals becomes an escort with multiple peaceful approaches.

events.idea: A field researcher has two water samples, one upstream and one downstream of a swarm nest. Help compare their debris before the current sweeps the evidence away.
events.why: Research across space becomes a quick environmental detective scene.

events.idea: A kelp scaffold has caught a vital supply case and is also sheltering small animals. The crew must lift the case without bringing the whole structure down.
events.why: Kelp's role as habitat complicates an otherwise straightforward salvage job.

events.idea: A wave ram has lodged sideways in the Crashing Waves passage, creating a temporary bridge that will break loose on the next surge.
events.why: A defeated hazard becomes a fleeting opportunity for traversal.

events.idea: Five malfunctioning underwater medicine lecturers each offer a different diagnosis for a broken pump; their clues collectively reveal a single loose connection.
events.why: The five short talks become an amusing group deduction with a useful repair.

events.idea: An abandoned enrichment puzzle holds a key inside. Solving it voluntarily opens the box, while forcing it triggers the nearby corrupted keeper.
events.why: The distinction between choice and compulsion gives a simple puzzle a thematic consequence.

events.idea: A patrol's noise is drowning out a distant rescue signal. The crew can shut down its buoys in sequence and listen as the signal becomes clearer.
events.why: Noise disturbance becomes a listening puzzle whose feedback is immediately audible.

events.idea: A sensory guide and a mobility guide disagree after a corridor floods; a stranded visitor needs a route that is both navigable and quiet.
events.why: The site's multiple ways of planning a visit become a route-finding problem with a human purpose.

events.idea: A salmon-cycle wheel is stuck between stages, repeatedly sweeping a walkway. A crew member can reset it while another times a crossing to reach the controls.
events.why: A life-cycle exhibit supplies a compact coordination challenge.

events.idea: The rooftop plant walk has become an improvised refuge. The crew can carry clean water up to it or use the same water to distract pursuing sampler drones.
events.why: The waterfront plant walk supplies a grounded refuge and a consequential resource choice.
